title: Conormal-kernel coordinates and a smooth zero slice
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $B$ a smooth finite-type $k$-algebra, $I\subset B$ an ideal and $\mathfrak p\supset I$ a prime. Put $A=B/I$, $M=\operatorname{Spec}B$, $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $x=\mathfrak p/I$, $L=\kappa(x)$ and $V=\Omega_{B/k}\otimes_BL$. Write $K$ for the kernel of the canonical surjection $V\to\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_AL$, and put $n=\dim_LV$, $r=\dim_LK$. There is an affine open neighbourhood $W\subset M$ of $\mathfrak p$ and functions $f_1,\ldots,f_r$ in the ideal of $X\cap W$ and $g_1,\ldots,g_{n-r}\in\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ such that the $df_i$ form a basis of $K$, and the $df_i,dg_j$ together form a basis of $V$. The coordinate map
$$e=(f_1,\ldots,f_r,g_1,\ldots,g_{n-r}):W\longrightarrow\mathbf A^n_k$$
is etale. The closed subscheme $M_0=V(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subset W$ contains $X\cap W$ and its map $(g_j):M_0\to\mathbf A^{n-r}_k$ is the base change of $e$ along the coordinate subspace $\mathbf A^{n-r}_k\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^n_k$; in particular $M_0$ is smooth over $k$. The canonical differential-fibre map identifies
$$\Omega_{M_0/k}\otimes L=V/\langle df_1,\ldots,df_r\rangle.$$
These assertions impose no smoothness or reducedness on $X$. For $r=0$ the zero slice is $W$. Here differentials, residue fields, affine space and base change are as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf], [def-weil-residue-field], [def-weil-module-base-change], [def-sbc-affine-space], [def-pc-base-change]; smoothness, finite type, closed immersions and etaleness are as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Smoothness of the algebra means [def-weil-pbc-smooth-ring-map].

proof.text: Apply the quotient conormal sequence to $k\to B\to A=B/I$: $(I/I^2)\to A\otimes_B\Omega_{B/k}\to\Omega_{A/k}\to0$, with $[f]\mapsto1\otimes df$. Tensor this right exact sequence over $A$ with $L$. Tensor associativity gives the exact sequence $(I/I^2)\otimes_A L\to V\to\Omega_{A/k}\otimes_A L\to0$. Thus $K$ is precisely the $L$-span of the classes $df\otimes1$, $f\in I$; there is no claim that the first arrow is injective.

By the definition of a smooth ring map, $\Omega_{B/k}$ is a direct summand of a finite free $B$-module; after tensoring the splitting with $L$, $V$ is a direct summand of a finite-dimensional $L$-space and hence finite-dimensional. Choose a maximal linearly independent subfamily of the spanning family $\{df\otimes1:f\in I\}$ of $K$. It has $r$ members, say $df_1,\ldots,df_r$, with $f_i\in I$. The presentation of Kähler differentials by symbols $db$ shows that $\{db\otimes1:b\in B\}$ spans $V$. Starting with these $r$ vectors, repeatedly append a member of this spanning family outside the span until it is all of $V$. This gives $g_1,\ldots,g_{n-r}\in B$ and the required basis $df_i,dg_j$. This is finite-dimensional basis selection, with no lifting of arbitrary $L$-linear combinations to functions.

source.place: Tag 00T2, definition-smooth; elementary basis selection from the symbol construction in Tag 00RM, section-differentials, preceding Tag 07BK, definition-differentials

proof.text: The affine smoothness comparison makes $M=\operatorname{Spec}B$ smooth over $k$; it is finite type by hypothesis. The affine differential-sheaf description and the associated-sheaf stalk localization theorem identify the fibre at $\mathfrak p$ with $V$, compatibly with $db$: the tensor identification is $(m/s)\otimes\ell\mapsto m\otimes s^{-1}\ell$, with inverse $m\otimes\ell\mapsto(m/1)\otimes\ell$. Here $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=\kappa(\mathfrak p/I)=L$: the prime-residue-field theorem identifies both with the fraction field of the same domain $B/\mathfrak p=A/x$. Apply the prescribed-differential-basis criterion to the global functions $(f_1,\ldots,f_r,g_1,\ldots,g_{n-r})$ on $M$. It produces an open neighbourhood $U$ of $\mathfrak p$ on which their map to $\mathbf A^n_k$ is etale. This uses no condition on $\Omega_{A/k}$ or on $X$.

source.place: Tag 01V6, lemma-smooth-characterize; Tag 02GU, lemma-etale-at-point (8), in the prescribed-coordinate form of lem-pur-etale-at-point-from-differentials

proof.text: Choose an affine open $W\subseteq U$ containing $\mathfrak p$ using the affine-open basis. Its inclusion into $U$ is an open immersion, hence etale, and composition shows that $e:W\to\mathbf A^n_k$ remains etale. Restrict all chosen functions to $W$ and put $C=\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$. By the defining restriction compatibility of the differential sheaf, the fibre at the marked point and all the chosen differential classes remain the ones already used in $V$. The germ-normalized stalk localization theorem and the tensor formula of Step 3 give these fibre identifications.

source.place: Tag 01IT, lemma-basis-affine-opens; morphisms.tex Tags 02GP, lemma-open-immersion-etale, and 02GN, lemma-composition-etale

proof.text: Let $J=(f_1,\ldots,f_r)\subseteq C$ and $M_0=\operatorname{Spec}(C/J)$. Each $f_i$ was in $I$, so its restriction vanishes on the scheme $X\cap W$, not just on its points. The map $C\to\Gamma(X\cap W,\mathcal O)$ therefore factors through $C/J$. The affine quotient description of a closed immersion shows that this is the claimed containment $X\cap W\subseteq M_0$. When $r=0$, $J=(0)$, so $M_0=W$.

source.place: Tag 01QO, lemma-closed-immersion; elementary factorization through a quotient ring

proof.text: Write $P=k[T_1,\ldots,T_n]$ and $Q=(T_1,\ldots,T_r)$. The coordinate subspace is $\operatorname{Spec}(P/Q)=\mathbf A^{n-r}_k$ with its remaining coordinates $T_{r+j}$. Under the coordinate map $P\to C$, $T_i\mapsto f_i$ and $T_{r+j}\mapsto g_j$, the extended ideal $QC$ is $J$. The tensor-quotient identification gives $C\otimes_P(P/Q)\cong C/J$. The affine fibre-product theorem thus identifies $M_0$ with $W\times_{\mathbf A^n_k}\mathbf A^{n-r}_k$. The second projection has coordinates $g_j\bmod J$, so it is precisely the stated map $(g_j)$.

source.place: Tags 01I4, lemma-fibre-product-affine-schemes, and 01JQ, lemma-fibre-product-affines; algebra.tex Tag 00DF, lemma-tensor-product-exact, for the tensor quotient

proof.text: By etale base change, $M_0\to\mathbf A^{n-r}_k$ is etale. An etale morphism is smooth, and $\mathbf A^{n-r}_k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth, so smoothness of compositions gives smoothness of $M_0/k$. All three results apply to the whole affine zero slice, not merely to its marked point.

source.place: Tag 02GO, lemma-base-change-etale; Tag 02GK, lemma-etale-smooth-unramified; Tag 01VA, lemma-composition-smooth; algebra.tex Tag 00T7, lemma-standard-smooth, for affine space

proof.text: Apply the same conormal exact sequence and tensor right exactness to $C\twoheadrightarrow C/J$ and its residue field $L$. It identifies the differential fibre of $M_0/k$ with the fibre of $\Omega_{C/k}$ modulo the span of $dh$, $h\in J$. If $h=\sum_i a_i f_i$, Leibniz gives $dh=\sum_i a_i\,df_i+\sum_i f_i\,da_i$. Since every $f_i$ vanishes at the marked point, the second sum has zero residue fibre; the first is in the span of the $df_i$. Conversely each $f_i$ lies in $J$, so the image is exactly that span. The affine differential-sheaf restriction compatibility identifies the fibre of $\Omega_{C/k}$ with $V$. The resulting quotient is therefore $V/\langle df_1,\ldots,df_r\rangle$, and its quotient map is the canonical differential map, since the conormal map sends $[h]$ to $dh$. No step assumed $X$ reduced or smooth. The germ-normalized stalk localization theorem and the tensor formula of Step 3 give these fibre identifications.
